The discussion detailed how convmem utilizes Ollama running at http://localhost:11434 to serve embeddings via nomic-embed-text and summarization through llama3.1:8b. For the synthesis or distill path, the system prefers deepseek-v4-flash accessed via DeepSeek API when DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is set. If that key is absent, the architecture automatically falls back to using the local llama3.1:8b instance for those specific workflows without external dependencies.
Keywords: convmem, Ollama, http://localhost:11434, nomic-embed-text, llama3.1:8b, deepseek-v4-flash, DeepSeek API, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY

The user reported a persistent 404 error on `/wp-login.php` within the staging2 environment caused by SiteGround Security plugin slug renaming conflicting with custom overrides in `wh-local-dev`. Investigation confirmed that local configuration changes were not applied to staging, requiring manual alignment of login slugs while verifying redirect functionality post-update. Resolution involved updating the SiteGround Security settings to match `wh-local-dev`, and the session was recorded as file identifier `dec_prop_20260624_025115_862b`.
Keywords: wp-login.php, staging2, SiteGround Security plugin, wh-local-dev, slug override, 404 error, redirect verification, dec_prop_20260624_025115_862b

We implemented a Thai Massage card morph on willowyhollow using the cross-document View Transition API via `document.startViewTransition`. A shared view-transition-name was applied to both the home card and the dedicated Thai Massage page, utilizing a cubic-bezier fade-forward curve for the animation. This implementation successfully created a smooth morph between cards while improving perceived performance and reducing Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).
Keywords: willowyhollow, View Transition API, document.startViewTransition, shared view-transition-name, cubic-bezier fade-forward curve, home card, Thai Massage page, CLS
